analysis.title: Gold Bulls Have One Big Problem
key_insights: The gold bull case is increasingly reduced to one driver: continued central-bank buying. The note asks who the next buyer is if the dollar rises and traditional macro tailwinds fade.
Gold is trading well below its 200-day moving average and is testing a major trend line. A close below the trend line brings the $4,000 level into play.
Gold has tracked the dollar closely since last autumn. Recent dollar strength has opened a wide gap versus gold, which implies another leg lower for gold.
Gold has not reacted to macro stress in France. The note says the 'buy gold when things get messy' framework does not always work.
GS expects gold to rise 23% through end-2027, and nearly all of that upside is attributed to central-bank purchases. The bull case therefore requires someone to keep paying a higher price.
Central-bank gold purchases are running at more than 5x the pre-2022 monthly average. GS assumes purchases average 60 tonnes/month through 2026-27.

Gold call positioning is around three times historical averages. GS argues this can amplify upside through dealer hedging, but the market is increasingly flow-driven and exposed if the underlying flow changes.
Gold skew is moving sharply higher as investors pay up for downside protection.
Bulls and bears converge on $4,000 as the key level. GS's hawkish scenario takes gold toward $4,070, and UBS says pullbacks toward $4,000 should be used to add.
